title: Eligibility for Healthier SG Enrolment for Those with Pre-existing Health Conditions
what_it_is: Eligibility for Healthier SG Enrolment for Those with Pre-existing Health Conditions

sections.label: Eligibility for enrolment
sections.summary: All Singapore residents aged 40 and above are eligible to enrol.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: All Singapore residents aged 40 and above are eligible to enrol.

sections.label: Enrolment and health plan
sections.summary: Residents aged 40 and above can enrol by going to general practitioners or polyclinics, where a health plan guides tests and follow-ups.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: For enrolment, as we have said, 40 and above, they can enrol.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Basically, they can go to general practitioners, they can go to polyclinics.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: But enrolment itself requires the act of actually going to the doctor to do the health plan.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: With that health plan, then your doctor can advise you on what are some of the tests you need to do, what are the further follow-ups, what are the things that you need to comply with.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: If there are chronic conditions that are existing, then there will also be more specific and more guided support provided by the Healthier SG primary care providers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: This is a separate consideration, because for each type of condition, the different screening comes into play depending on conditions.

sections.label: Surfacing cases of unsupported patients
sections.summary: Patients lacking needed support or denied screening due to ineligibility could surface such cases for review.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: If there are some specific conditions where patients feel that they are not getting the support that they need, or they are needing to go for certain screening and they are not allowed to because they are ineligible, perhaps she could surface some of those cases and we could take a look.
